answer: Plant canary tasks in the trellis of ordinary work: assignments indistinguishable from real ones whose ground truth only the network knows. A single operator driving many identities over the same ridge will repeat the same wrong answer on the canaries, while honest workers' errors scatter in different directions. Read through that prism, correlated failure is a fingerprint no script can hide, and a cluster caught sharing canary errors is quarantined as one operator — so each extra copy raises the chance the whole set is exposed.
